label: Koto
notes: A session builds the whole engine (nothing shared between sessions), applies its limits, registers the host call function, then evaluates 1 + 1 and reads 2 back in Rust. Limits: KotoSettings::with_execution_limit(600s) (wall-clock deadline checked between instructions); io and os modules removed from the prelude (Koto's default prelude has file I/O and os.command); no memory or instruction-count limit API; `import` can still load .koto files from disk (no setting disables it).
Memory: resident growth across 1,000 live sessions (stopped by target), measured first in a fresh process.

Tool call: the guest calls a registered Rust function on its own stack. Median of per-batch means, 1,000,000 calls in batches of 1,000 after 100,000 warm-ups; mean 0.7902 µs, slowest batch 1.1768 µs per call; 0.7902 µs of CPU per call.
Session = Koto::with_settings (fresh core-library prelude per runtime) minus io/os, plus prelude call.
Host fn is KMap::add_fn("call", |ctx| ...) on the prelude; reply keys reuse preallocated KStrings.
Guest is an exported Koto function invoked with Koto::call_function.
Compute: not measured in the Rust host.
